newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: More than 300 may benefit from $9 mln will.
newsitem.headline: More than 300 may benefit from $9 mln will.

text.p: More than 300 people may benefit from the Singapore $13 million (US$9.3 million) estate of a Singaporean businessman who died over 70 years ago, The Straits Times newspaper reported on Friday.

The newspaper said that when Seah Liang Seah died in 1925, his will stipulated that his assets could not be distributed until 21 years after the death of the last surviving child of the then King of England, George the Fifth.
This turned out to be the Duke of Gloucester, who died in 1974.
The contents of the will are not what is being argued about in court. The problem is, who are the beneficiaries? Seah is estimated to have over 300 descendents.
For example, Singapore's High Court must rule whether the beneficiaries include adopted or illegitimate children, or those who have been made bankrupt.
The lawyers will be back in court on Friday.
